intent: Give kuhylog (~/kuhylog/kuhylog) an on-style launcher icon from the shared family, replacing the stock Flutter logo it was still shipping. Registers it as app #11 with a new track-bars glyph.
scope: python_pkg/app_icons/glyphs.py: adds the _TRACK_BARS fragment and its GLYPHS entry
python_pkg/app_icons/apps.py: adds the kuhylog AppIcon registry entry
Non-goal: no change to style.py, the renderer, or any existing app's icon - a style change would restyle the whole family
Non-goal: no iOS assets; kuhylog has no ios/ target at all (android/ and linux/ only)
changes: Three rising bars with a hollow plotted point above the tallest: a day-by-day log that adds up to a trend, which is what the app records. Distinct from the existing ten glyphs at a glance.

Bars are strokes rather than filled rects so the glyph carries one stroke weight throughout, unlike the filled anvil/quill-nib silhouettes. At a 168px pitch the 72px strokes leave 96px gaps, well above MIN_NEGATIVE_SPACE, so they stay separate at 48dp instead of merging into a block.
The marker sits on its own row above the tallest bar cap rather than beside it, so the two never collide, and is hollow so it reads as a data point rather than a full stop.
Registered with linux=True: a Linux desktop target was added to kuhylog in the same session, and it ships desktop/icons plus a desktop entry.
Accent is the shared #B8862E, matching all ten existing apps - apps are distinguished by glyph shape, not colour.

verification.evidence: All hooks Passed or Skipped, including ruff, ruff format, mypy, pylint, bandit, codespell, 'Block binary/image files' and 'check for leaked secrets'. 'pytest with coverage enforcement' reported 1309 passed and TOTAL 100% across python_pkg.

44 passed; every app_icons module at 100% branch coverage (apps.py, glyphs.py, cli.py, generate.py, preview.py, render.py, style.py, __main__.py). The registry tests are invariant-based with no hardcoded app/glyph counts, so they cover the new entry without edits.

Wrote 6 asset files and regenerated the Android mipmaps with no safe-box warning. mipmap-hdpi/ic_launcher.png md5 changed from the stock 13e9c72ec37fac220397aa819fa1ef2d to c5fee3fe7667ae24d38af75ee313ee28, and mipmap-anydpi-v26/ic_launcher.xml now exists. First run failed until flutter_launcher_icons was added to the app's pubspec (skill step 5), which is expected.
Wrote 8 hicolor PNGs (16..512). Placed under desktop/icons to match home_inventory/todo/diet-guard, not the linux/icons path the skill text suggests.
Inspected the three rows (full size, circle-masked, 48dp). track-bars is rightmost, legible at 48dp, and sits with the family in weight and colour.
The icon inside the built APK is the new glyph on the charcoal field. Installed APK md5 matches the local build byte for byte, so the shipped artifact is correct.

risks: Glyph legibility is a visual judgement; checked on the preview sheet at 48dp and by viewing the icon extracted from the APK, not asserted by a test.

The launcher on the physical device (Pixel 6a, nexuslauncher) still drew the stock Flutter logo in the app drawer after `adb install -r`. The APK provably contains the new icon, so this is the launcher's stale icon cache, which the app-icon skill already warns about. Force-stopping nexuslauncher did not visibly refresh it within the session; not confirmed resolved on-device.

app-icon/SKILL.md still documents charcoal #1B1D21 and accent #4C7DF0, which the live generator and all eleven registered apps contradict (#211D1B / #B8862E). Following the skill text literally would produce an off-palette icon. Still not fixed - same finding as the anvil/octoforge artifact.
rollback: git revert the commit; it only adds a glyph and a registry entry, so nothing else depends on it.
After rollback, run python3 -m python_pkg.app_icons list and confirm ten apps and ten glyphs, then re-run the app_icons test suite.
kuhylog's already-generated icon assets live in its own repo and are unaffected by a revert here; regenerating them would then fail with 'unknown app kuhylog', which is the expected signal.
